page: Microsoft Azure DC16s_v3 is a dedicated x86_64 server instance belonging to the DCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the DC16s_v3 consistently in the average tier across most standard workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1898.0 and a multi-core score of 30343.46, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 30808.33. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1687.72 GB/sec, which drops to 143.02 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write bandwidth of 60.51 GB/sec. Notably, the server shows strong performance in Geekbench image processing and small-model LLM text generation. However, it exhibits weak performance in large-model LLM prompt processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the DC16s_v3 offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive operations without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The dedicated physical core allocation ensures consistent compute performance, making it suitable for workloads that require predictable execution. This server is best suited for memory-optimized applications, database operations, software compilation, and moderate-scale web serving or text processing tasks.
